question.problem: Given the hyperboloid of one sheet $(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{9}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ (x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-1 & =\frac{{z}^{2}}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2} & =9((x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-1) \\ z & =\pm 3\sqrt{(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-1 & \ge 0 \\ (x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exterior of the ellipse $(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1,$ which includes the boundary.

Therefore, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\,:\,(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}\ge 1\}.
$$
